episodes.184244: A severe thunderstorm impacted the Humble area, resulting in damage to power lines from strong wind gusts.
episodes.184368: A humid air mass was filtering into the local islands from the east. This area of inclement weather resulted in an increase in frequency of showers and thunderstorms. Under an unstable atmosphere, additional convective development was observed in the south of Puerto Rico in the afternoon hours. One of these storms generated a funnel cloud.
episodes.184404: Showers and thunderstorms developed across portions of Middle Tennessee on September 27, 2023. While these were generally non-severe, one thunderstorm near Murfreesboro became briefly severe with a 60 mph wind gust measured which downed a tree on a nearby college campus.
episodes.184763: A nearly stationary frontal boundary draped across central Illinois served as the focusing mechanism for clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms during the evening of September 26th.  The storms grew more numerous and vigorous as the nocturnal low-level jet nosed into the region.  As a result, a few of the cells were able to produce damaging wind gusts of around 60 mph and hail as large as quarters.
episodes.185538: An ordinary/single-cell thunderstorm produced an apparent downburst near the community of Woodward, leading to a few reports of wind damage/gusts.
episodes.185826: Isolated thunderstorms developed as an upper level shortwave trough moved over the region. One of these storms produced severe wind gusts.
episodes.185983: A weakening upper-level trough over the Florida Peninsula created an early start for convection as showers and storms began to develop in the morning hours over the Atlantic Ocean.
episodes.187149: A stalled surface boundary extending from near Kansas City through central Illinois provided a focus for organized convection during the afternoon. Thunderstorms were mainly hail producers, with up to 1.75 inch diameter hailstones reported in the St. Louis metropolitan area.

events.narrative: Multiple power poles along the US-59 frontage road near the Deerbrook Mall were downed by strong thunderstorm wind gusts.

An intensifying discrete thunderstorm produced quarter sized hail along I-70 in Warren County. This storm went on to produce up to golf ball sized hail just after crossing the border into St. Charles County.

The thunderstorm that produced quarter sized hail in Warren County intensified quickly as it entered St. Charles County. There were numerous reports of severe hail in and around Wentzville, ranging from quarters to golf balls. Hailstones damaged windows and siding in multiple neighborhoods in Wentzville before weakening after passing the city.
A discrete thunderstorm produced sub-severe hail in Warren County before crossing the border into Franklin County and dropping quarter sized hail between Washington and Pacific.
The discrete thunderstorm that produced severe hail in Franklin County produced wind damage in Jefferson County. A trained spotter reported a snapped power pole in Cedar Hill.
A few 5 to 6-inch diameter tree limbs were blown down.
A tree was blown down near the intersection of Townline Road and Towerline Road.
A few tree limbs were blown down.
An emergency manager reported a brief funnel cloud over Highway A1A in Jupiter as a shower passed through the area.
Image relayed showing electrical pole leaning. Time estimated based on radar imagery and nearby wind gust at Woodward (WOOD) Mesonet site.
A report from the public and broadcast media indicated that a funnel cloud was observed from PFC Santos Cruz Aviles in Salinas.

An AWOS station at the Murfreesboro Municipal Airport measured a 60 mph thunderstorm wind gust. At nearby Middle Tennessee State University, a tree and several branches were downed. Damages for the tree and branches are a rough estimate.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts measured at 68 mph by the ASOS at the Laughlin AFB Auxiliary field near Spofford.
